{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. Of the eighteen rules tested, eleven clauses are compliant (several at our preferred position, not merely the fallback) and seven are deviations requiring redlines. Six of the seven deviations are material enough to sit in walk-away territory as currently drafted.

The critical issue is indemnification: § 20 contains a one-way Customer indemnity covering "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services", and there is no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement. This is compounded by § 21.1, which caps each Party's liability at one month of Fees "without exception", overriding the Excluded Claims that § 21.3 already defines.

Three clauses impose competitive and volume restraints that our playbook does not accept: full-term exclusivity (§ 2.2), a 24-month post-term non-compete of undefined scope (§ 12.4), and a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment stripped of any reduction or termination right (§ 2.1). Notably, each of these contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. We are relying on § 12.3 as drafting support, but internal inconsistency is not a cure and the § 2.2 order-of-precedence clause does not resolve conflicts within the Agreement itself.

Two further deviations are narrower: § 13.1 grants the Services licence to "Customer alone", excluding Affiliates and contractors and making the licence revocable at Vendor's sole discretion (contradicting §§ 13.2, 13.3 and 24.1); and § 11.1 requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data (contradicting §§ 11.2 and 11.3). § 19.2's fifteen-day Deliverable warranty is below our floor and, as drafted, arguably cuts off correction and refund obligations generally.

On the credit side, the IP and Customer Data package (§§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4, 15.1), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9.4), renewal and price uplift (§§ 8.2–8.3), audit (§ 22), insurance (§ 18), governing law and venue (§ 28) all meet our preferred position, and there are no Customer-payable liquidated damages, MFN or non-solicitation obligations anywhere in the document.

One housekeeping point: § 9.3 cross-refers to "the remedies required by Section 20.5", which does not exist. That dangling reference should be resolved as part of the indemnity negotiation.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 20 (esp. 20.1); cf. §§ 9.3, 19.4–19.5, 21.3, 29.2 | One-way Customer indemnity for "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services"; no Vendor indemnity anywhere. Walk-away. Insert Vendor defence/indemnity (IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation procedure, and narrow our indemnity. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4, 15.1, 1.8 | Preferred position met: present assignment of Deliverables, Vendor retained rights confined to Vendor Technology, perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence back, Customer owns Customer Data with processing-only rights for Vendor. No redline. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2; cf. § 12.3 | Vendor as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics for the full term, no category limit, no 12-month cap, no performance-based exit. Walk-away; fails fallback on every material term. Convert to non-exclusive. |
| 4 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4; cf. § 12.3 | 24-month post-term non-compete of undefined scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory"). Walk-away. Strike as intentionally omitted, relying on § 12.3. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 13.1; cf. §§ 13.2, 13.3, 24.1 | Licence to "Customer alone", expressly excluding Affiliates and contractors, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion. Walk-away; fails fallback. Extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf; revocation only for uncured material breach; delete "non-transferable". |
| 6 | High | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 11.1; cf. §§ 11.2, 11.3, 10.1 | Immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data, no export or migration support; no transition period anywhere. Walk-away. Replace with up to six months' assistance at then-current rates; anchor § 11.2's 30-day return to expiry or termination. |
| 7 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4, 13.3, 1.1 | Preferred position met: Customer free to assign to Affiliate/successor; Vendor assignment and change of control require our consent; no Vendor termination, repricing or acceleration on our change of control. Minor wording points noted only. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4; cf. §§ 9.1–9.5, 8.2–8.3, 27.3, 24.4 | Preferred position met: 30 days' notice, whole or partial, refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right during a committed term. Tension with § 2.1 take-or-pay is addressed under MINCOMMIT. |
| 9 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 9.4; cf. §§ 27.3, 7.3, 21.3 | No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee or acceleration anywhere. Preferred position met. |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2.1; cf. §§ 12.3, 9.4, 7.1, 22.2–22.3 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right. Walk-away; short of fallback. Narrow to current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, shortfall handled by true-up. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 19.2; cf. §§ 19.1, 19.3, 19.4, 1.7 | Fifteen-day Deliverable conformance period with an unqualified post-period cut-off of correction and refund obligations; below the 90-day floor and arguably cuts off § 19.1 remedies. Extend to 90 days and scope the cut-off to that Deliverable. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §§ 22.1–22.3 | Preferred position met: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor bears costs absent >5% underpayment, no direct system access. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 | New York law; exclusive jurisdiction in New York County state and federal courts; no arbitration provision; customary injunctive-relief carve-out only. |
| 14 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 12.3; cf. §§ 7.1, 8.3 | No MFN/MFC, benchmarking or right-to-match obligation; § 12.3 expressly confirms none. Pricing obligations run in our favour. |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No solicitation, no-hire or inducement covenant on Customer; § 12.3 preserves general-recruitment hiring. § 12.4 is addressed under NONCOMPETE. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §§ 8.2–8.3 | Preferred position met: successive 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%, no increase on prepaid periods. |
| 17 | Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 21.1; cf. §§ 21.2, 21.3, 1.5 | One month of Fees "without exception", below the 12-month fallback and our 6-month floor, and overriding the § 21.3 Excluded Claims. Set a mutual 12-month cap expressly subject to Excluded Claims. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 18.1–18.2 | Preferred position met: CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber and privacy 5M, workers' compensation, employer's liability, one-year tail, primary coverage, certificates on request. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory as drafted and must be resolved before signature:

1. **No Vendor indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity (§ 20.1).** Vendor accepts no defence obligation for IP infringement of its own Services or Deliverables, while we indemnify it for "every claim relating in any way to" our use of those Services. This must be reversed to a mutual, properly scoped allocation.
2. **Full-term exclusivity (§ 2.2).** Exclusive dealing for the entire term, with no category limit, no 12-month cap and no exit for service-level or delivery failures.
3. **24-month post-term non-compete of undefined scope (§ 12.4).** Restricts us from developing, marketing, selling or acquiring any competing product or service in any territory for two years after the term.
4. **Three-year take-or-pay with no exit (§ 2.1).** USD 2,000,000 per year, expressly "without reduction or termination rights", which also undercuts our § 9.4 convenience-termination right.
5. **Licence to "Customer alone", revocable at Vendor's discretion (§ 13.1).** Affiliates and contractors are excluded with no path to add them, and the licence can be pulled at will.
6. **Immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data (§ 11.1).** No export or migration support, and no transition assistance period anywhere in the Agreement.

The § 21.1 one-month liability cap "without exception" also falls below our 6-month floor and neutralises the § 21.3 Excluded Claims; while graded low severity, we do not expect to sign without the 12-month mutual cap and Excluded Claims carve-out.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven deviations, in the following order of priority:
   - § 20 — insert Vendor defence and indemnity (IP infringement of the Services or Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with a notice, control and cooperation procedure; narrow Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of Applicable Law.
   - § 21.1 — mutual cap of twelve (12) months' Fees, expressly subject to the § 21.3 Excluded Claims.
   - § 2.2 — convert to a non-exclusive appointment (also aligning with § 12.3).
   - § 12.4 — strike the post-term non-compete as intentionally omitted, relying on § 12.3.
   - § 2.1 — narrow the take-or-pay to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
   - § 13.1 — extend the Services licence to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf; replace discretionary revocation with termination only for uncured material breach; delete "non-transferable" to remove the conflict with the § 13.3 transfer right.
   - § 11.1 / § 11.2 — up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates; anchor the 30-day machine-readable data return to expiry or termination (retaining the request trigger).
   - § 19.2 — extend fifteen days to ninety (90) days and scope the post-period cut-off to that Deliverable only.
2. **Flag the fallbacks in comments** where Vendor resists: for indemnity, an IP indemnity with customary modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies and a 3x annual fee super-cap.
3. **Resolve the dangling cross-reference** in § 9.3 to "the remedies required by Section 20.5", which does not exist, at the same time as the § 20 indemnity negotiation.
4. **Raise the internal inconsistencies** between § 12.3 and §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4, and between § 13.1 and §§ 13.2/13.3/24.1, and between § 11.1 and §§ 11.2/11.3, so that the accepted edits leave a coherent document rather than competing provisions.
5. **Note for the business team**, without redlining: no express 12-month software conformance period in § 19; § 19.3's malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor"; the § 21.1 cap remains on an "actually paid" basis with no USD 1,000,000 floor; and the § 21.3 payment carve-out is limited to "undisputed Fees for conforming Services".
6. **Escalate the walk-away items** to the deal sponsor before the next negotiation session so that we have a clear mandate on the exclusivity, non-compete and take-or-pay package."}
